title: The Boroughs
synopsis: Your retirement community is, unfortunately, haunted by something. You and your bridge club — none of you under seventy-three — have agreed to investigate. Your hearing aids have new uses.

nodes.text: Lila finishes a hand and announces, calmly, that she heard the spirit again last night at 2:14 a.m. The other three of you put down your cards because Lila is never wrong about times.

choices.text: Take her seriously immediately
choices.consequence: You take her seriously immediately. The way toward The Old Map opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Ask kind, clarifying questions first
choices.consequence: You commit to ask kind, clarifying questions first. It carries you into The Hearing Aids while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Marvin produces, from his apartment, a 1962 map of the original property — a sanatorium before it was the retirement village. Three rooms on the map no longer exist on the current floor plan. The paths divide here: “Find the rooms” leads into The Three Rooms, while “Research what happened in them first” makes The Librarian the next reckoning.

choices.text: Find the rooms
choices.consequence: You find the rooms. The way toward The Three Rooms opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Research what happened in them first
choices.consequence: You commit to research what happened in them first. It carries you into The Librarian while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Beverly's new hearing aids pick up frequencies the rest of yours don't. She agrees to wear them tonight at 2:14. The four of you have, accidentally, become an investigative unit. Choose “Set up an overnight stakeout” and The Three Rooms comes into view; choose “Set up a microphone array instead” and the road bends toward The Librarian.

choices.text: Set up an overnight stakeout
choices.consequence: You commit to set up an overnight stakeout. It carries you into The Three Rooms while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Set up a microphone array instead
choices.consequence: You set up a microphone array instead. The way toward The Librarian opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Two of the three rooms are inside the current basement wall. One of them, you realize after a long Saturday morning, is behind the laundry room. Behind the dryer is a door that is, distinctly, painted over.

choices.text: Open the door
choices.consequence: You commit to open the door. It carries you into Inside the Door while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Photograph the door and call the property manager
choices.consequence: You commit to photograph the door and call the property manager. It carries you into Detective Petrillo while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The paths divide here: “Bring this to the property manager” leads into Inside the Door, while “Bring it to the police as a cold case” makes Detective Petrillo the next reckoning. In The Librarian, even a sensible delay gives the threat another way in.

choices.text: Bring this to the property manager
choices.consequence: You commit to bring this to the property manager. It carries you into Inside the Door while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Bring it to the police as a cold case
choices.consequence: You choose to bring it to the police as a cold case. By Detective Petrillo, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The hidden room contains an old hospital bed, two chairs, and a small brass key. The room is cold in a way the basement is not. You realize, sweetly, that you are not scared. You are interested.

choices.text: Take the key out and try other locks
choices.consequence: You choose to take the key out and try other locks. By The Brass Key, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Leave the key; document the room
choices.consequence: You commit to leave the key; document the room. It carries you into The Microphone Pickup while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: A young detective named Petrillo agrees to take this seriously — partly because his grandmother lives in your building, mostly because Marvin is, unbelievably, his father's old high school teacher. “Work with him formally” draws you toward The Brass Key; “Share what you've found and step back” leaves The Microphone Pickup waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Work with him formally
choices.consequence: You commit to work with him formally. It carries you into The Brass Key while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Share what you've found and step back
choices.consequence: You choose to share what you've found and step back. By The Microphone Pickup, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The key fits a cabinet in the basement laundry. Inside is a small box of letters from a nurse named Eleanor. The letters describe a 'patient' the hospital was treating off the books in 1958.

choices.text: Read every letter aloud over tea
choices.consequence: You read every letter aloud over tea. The way toward Eleanor's Story opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Take them to the historical society
choices.consequence: You take them to the historical society. The way toward The Voice, Identified opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: At 2:14 a.m. Beverly's hearing aids pick up, clear as day, a woman's voice saying 'tell them about me.' Lila, sitting beside her, hears it too. You hear, faintly, something. Marvin is, blessedly, recording.

choices.text: Identify whose voice it is
choices.consequence: You choose to identify whose voice it is. By Eleanor's Story, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Sit with the request and decide who to tell
choices.consequence: You choose to sit with the request and decide who to tell. By The Voice, Identified, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You piece together, over three weeks of bridge nights, that Nurse Eleanor was protecting a patient — a young woman placed by her family in the sanatorium for 'hysteria' that was, more likely, queerness — and that Eleanor disappeared after smuggling her out.

choices.text: Find descendants of the patient
choices.consequence: You choose to find descendants of the patient. By The Granddaughter, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Find Eleanor's descendants
choices.consequence: You find Eleanor's descendants. The way toward The Plaque Committee opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: The voice is Eleanor's. You find a 1962 recording of her at a community meeting and confirm by tone. Eleanor, even in death, would like the record to include her sacrifice. Choose “Hold a small memorial” and The Granddaughter comes into view; choose “Get Eleanor's name on a plaque at the property” and the road bends toward The Plaque Committee.

choices.text: Hold a small memorial
choices.consequence: You choose to hold a small memorial. By The Granddaughter, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Get Eleanor's name on a plaque at the property
choices.consequence: You commit to get Eleanor's name on a plaque at the property. It carries you into The Plaque Committee while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Eleanor's granddaughter, in her sixties, lives in Cleveland. She comes to visit. She has never been told what her grandmother did. You sit her at a bridge table and tell her, slowly, all of it.

choices.text: Help her write a family history book
choices.consequence: You commit to help her write a family history book. It carries you into The Plaque Unveiling while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Just let her sit with it for the weekend
choices.consequence: You choose to just let her sit with it for the weekend. By The Book, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: The retirement village board, mostly seventy-year-olds, votes seven to two to put up a small plaque honoring Eleanor in the front lobby. The two no votes are, you suspect, motivated by laziness rather than principle.

choices.text: Write the plaque text yourself
choices.consequence: You commit to write the plaque text yourself. It carries you into The Plaque Unveiling while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Get the historical society to write it
choices.consequence: You choose to get the historical society to write it. By The Book, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Eleanor's granddaughter unveils the plaque on a Saturday in spring. The four of you wear your best clothes. The voice, at 2:14 a.m. that night, does not return. You realize, gently, that it doesn't need to.

choices.text: Form a permanent local history committee
choices.consequence: You choose to form a permanent local history committee. By The Next Mystery, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Go back to bridge
choices.consequence: You commit to go back to bridge. It carries you into The Quiet Year while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You and Marvin and Lila and Beverly help Eleanor's granddaughter write a small book. It is published by a regional press. It outsells the local cookbook. It is, by your measurements, a real success. Choose “Tour the book at three libraries” and The Next Mystery comes into view; choose “Donate the proceeds to a queer youth center” and the road bends toward The Quiet Year.

choices.text: Tour the book at three libraries
choices.consequence: You choose to tour the book at three libraries. By The Next Mystery, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Donate the proceeds to a queer youth center
choices.consequence: Continue Eleanor's work. You donate the proceeds to a queer youth center. The way toward The Quiet Year opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Petrillo, the detective, drops by with another cold case. Lila and Marvin and Beverly look at each other. You realize, with delight, that the bridge club has accidentally become an institution. Beverly's Cataract Surgery will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Take the next case” than after “Tell Petrillo this was the case.”

choices.text: Take the next case
choices.consequence: You take the next case. The way toward Beverly's Cataract Surgery opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Tell Petrillo this was the case
choices.consequence: You choose to tell Petrillo this was the case. By Beverly's Cataract Surgery, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You go back to bridge. The cards are familiar. The laughs come more easily. Eleanor, you realize, has done something good for the building — not by haunting it, but by being remembered. Marvin's Granddaughter Visits is already waiting. What changes is whether “Keep her photo on the wall above the bridge table” or “Move on; she's at peace” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.text: Keep her photo on the wall above the bridge table
choices.consequence: You commit to keep her photo on the wall above the bridge table. It carries you into Marvin's Granddaughter Visits while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Move on; she's at peace
choices.consequence: You commit to move on; she's at peace. It carries you into Marvin's Granddaughter Visits while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Beverly has surgery. She comes back to bridge with sharper eyes and the same hearing aids. She makes a joke about being able to read your bids now. You realize how lucky you are to keep getting to play.

choices.text: Celebrate with cake
choices.consequence: You celebrate with cake. The way toward The Next Hand opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Just deal the next hand
choices.consequence: You choose to just deal the next hand. By The Next Hand, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Marvin's granddaughter, eight, comes to play a hand. She is too young for bridge so you teach her gin. She is, in two hands, beating you. The room fills with a sound you have not heard often — a child's laugh.

choices.text: Invite her to a recurring family-day Sunday
choices.consequence: You invite her to a recurring family-day Sunday. The way toward The Next Hand opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Send her home full of cookies and let it be one day
choices.consequence: You commit to send her home full of cookies and let it be one day. It carries you into The Next Hand while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: It is your deal. You shuffle. You look at three friends who are still here. You decide what kind of year is next — more cases, or more cake. Choose “Take the next case from Petrillo” and The Listening Society comes into view; choose “Cake. Just cake.” and the road bends toward Bridge, Tuesdays.

choices.text: Take the next case from Petrillo
choices.consequence: You take the next case from Petrillo. The way toward The Listening Society opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Cake. Just cake.
choices.consequence: Bridge Tuesdays forever. You commit to cake. Just cake. It carries you into Bridge, Tuesdays while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The four of you (eventually three, then two, then memory) become a small local legend. Other retirement villages start their own listening societies. You leave behind a quiet, devoted, weird little legacy. The road into The Listening Society began with “Take the next case from Petrillo” in The Next Hand; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You play bridge on Tuesdays for the rest of your life. The voice doesn't come back. You and your friends grow old together, slowly. You realize the haunting was, partly, an invitation. You took it. You're grateful you did.
